# Documents

Each document under docs/ says in its front matter what it is (tools/docs.py). Superseded ones
are left out here; each names what replaced it. docs/upstream/ holds others' text, as fetched.

## Current

How blaze is now. Kept true: CI checks their links, paths and settings against the tree.

- [benchmarks.md](benchmarks.md): How long an edit takes to build, the memory and disk it uses and how fast its programs run, against cargo, on three platforms.
- [borrowck.md](borrowck.md): blaze's own borrow checker (hir-ty-borrowck): how it matches rustc's verdicts, how it is scored, what is left.
- [cargo.md](cargo.md): Every blaze command and setting: cargo's commands and flags, what a build does, sandboxing, manifests.
- [const.md](const.md): Const evaluation: blaze's own interpreter for constants and const fns, and what it covers.
- [contributing.md](contributing.md): How to build, test and change blaze: AI use, where new code goes, rules for code, working in parallel, landing.
- [fuzzing.md](fuzzing.md): The fuzzers: generated programs and edits, each held to blaze's own build from nothing (a warm daemon, a warm store), what a finding is, and what they do not cover.
- [harness.md](harness.md): The harnesses that test blaze (real crates' own tests, and blaze held to itself), what each checks, and how CI runs them.
- [install.md](install.md): Installing blaze: the install script, the release channels and what gets installed.
- [mir-passes.md](mir-passes.md): The MIR passes from built MIR to runtime MIR, ported from rustc, that codegen and the interpreter run on.
- [release.md](release.md): Releases: the canary and stable channels, how a release is cut and what gates promotion to stable.
- [resolve.md](resolve.md): Reading Cargo.toml and .cargo/config.toml as cargo does (blaze-manifest), and how it measured against cargo.
- [toolchain.md](toolchain.md): blaze's own pinned nightly: what it is, how it is fetched and checked, and the daily bump.
- [usage.md](usage.md): Getting started: using blaze on a project, in short.
- [v2/plan/lanes/filters/speed-of-light.md](v2/plan/lanes/filters/speed-of-light.md): Lane filters - where a definite no in front of a membership test skips real work in blaze v2, the one site that pays (trait impls read only from the crates that can name the trait and the type), its bound and bench, and the sites checked and left as they are.
- [v2/plan/lanes/may-suspend/fiber-boundary.md](v2/plan/lanes/may-suspend/fiber-boundary.md): the blaze lint `blaze::fiber_boundary` (crates/blaze-lints/src/blaze/fiber.rs) rejects a path to `blaze_graph::sched::fiber`, corosensei or the fiber driver written outside `blaze_graph::sched`, so fibers stay the scheduler's alone; blaze's tree is to deny it from the workspace's `[workspace.metadata.blaze.lints]`.

The relations are views maintained on the write side by deltas, DBSP-style, and published as salsa inputs, one per slice, so an edit costs work proportional to the facts it changes and a reader sees a change only when its slice changed.

- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-macho-unwind.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-macho-unwind.md) (2026-10-29): Speed of the Mach-O `__unwind_info` builder (`crates/blaze-link/src/macho/unwind.rs`), which runs on every full and incremental link - lld's and ld64's way of building it, how the builder compared before the 2026-10-29 pass (allocations, passes, bytes per entry), what changed, and what it would take to shrink Rust code's tables further.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-macho-input.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-macho-input.md) (2026-10-29): The Mach-O object and archive readers (`macho/input.rs`, `macho/archive.rs`) against mold, wild, ld-prime and lld; what they cost before and after, and what the contract still forces.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-macho-dylib.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-macho-dylib.md) (2026-10-29): The Mach-O `.tbd` and dylib readers brought to the speed bar on 2026-10-29 — a SWAR lexer onto a flat tape of spans, lists filtered before decoding, names hashed once, the export trie walked with one name buffer — each compared with lld's TextAPI, mold and simdjson, and what the contract still costs.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-live.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-live.md) (2026-10-29): How blaze-live applies a patch fast (one read of the message into a reused buffer, viewed in place, a pool of four tables brought between generations by their cells, one release store, page runs written once, a watcher thread instead of 5 ms polling), the safety audit's answers (memory a patch never writes again, image checks), before and after per patch, what it measures against, and what is left; nothing in it was built or run.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-live-safety.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-live-safety.md) (2026-10-29): How blaze-live answers the safety audit for real, not by comment: v1 writes its jumps and statics with every other thread stopped and none inside the bytes (refusing the patch naming the function otherwise), its patch room is claimed before anything is mapped, every address, FDE and function table of a patch is bounds-checked with checked_add before a view or write, slots writes data by atomic stores, unsafe is confined to the platform modules, and what the linker still owes; nothing in it was built or run.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-hot-live.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-hot-live.md) (2026-10-29): The per-patch allocations of blaze-live's v1 runtime (the plan's bytes, its address sets, /proc/self/maps, FDE lists, the published process text) moved into buffers kept from patch to patch, the v2 switch held to zero allocations warm by a budget test, and every other allocation, clone and dyn in the crate justified as setup, error path or edge; before and after, counted from the code, nothing built or run.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-elf.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/speed-link-edge-elf.md) (2026-10-29): The ELF writer and readers of blaze-link against mold and wild, phase by phase, before and after speed-link-edge-elf.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link/notes.md](v2/plan/lanes/link/notes.md) (2026-10-29): How blaze-link works as written by lane link (the core, the jump table, positions, live patching, native resolution, PE and wasm rules) and what it still lacks; nothing in it was built or run.
- [v2/plan/lanes/link.md](v2/plan/lanes/link.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the parallel in-place linker and live patching.
- [v2/plan/lanes/items/speed-types.md](v2/plan/lanes/items/speed-types.md) (2026-10-29): speed pass over blaze-items' keys, hashes and facts (speed-types): item keys in rustc's DefPathHash shape so a key resolves with one lookup, batched preimages in one buffer, names hashed in place, against rustc's DefPathHash, Unison's component hashing and BLAKE3 batching.

- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/speed-of-light.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/speed-of-light.md) (2026-10-29): lane frontend's speed of light: for each component, the bound its work and the hardware set, the arithmetic, how the design reaches 90% of it, and what stands in the way where it does not yet.

- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/nameres-oracle.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/nameres-oracle.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-nameres-oracle — the invalidation oracle's cases for frontend.md items 1-3, fixture slots and blaze-v2-proof's `nameres` checks on build traces, rounds-independent.

- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/nameres-graph.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/nameres-graph.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-nameres-graph — the over-approximated import graph of an expansion round, its strongly connected components by Pearce's iterative algorithm over CSR edges, every case of the over-approximation and why it is sound, its speed-of-light bound, and what each test proves.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/nameres-diff.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/nameres-diff.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-nameres-diff — the proof that the per-module resolver (`facts::collect_crate`, `facts::collect_block`) builds the old collector's def maps, on every name resolution and macro expansion fixture and on generated crates, and that an edit reruns only the queries whose facts changed.

- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/windows.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/windows.md) (2026-10-29): The Windows journal of changes (frontend-journal-windows) - the NTFS/ReFS USN journal read unprivileged from a saved USN and journal ID, overlapped on the completion port, with reference numbers made names through a lazy map of directories, removals told as Lost::Unnamed directories, and stamps and listings by handle and FileIdBothDirectoryInfo - compared with how Everything and watchman read the journal.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/tree.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/tree.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 opens the VFS tree in place from the daemon's image (frontend-journal-tree) - the store's mapped base generation, files as image ranges checked by page group on first read, a journal that starts with a base record naming the image and holds only the tail, crash-safe across the image's rename and the journal's rewrite - its speed of light, and how it compares with git's index and Sapling's treestate.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/macos.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/macos.md) (2026-10-29): The macOS journal of changes (frontend-journal-macos) - an FSEvents stream started sinceWhen a saved event ID, checked against the volume store's UUID, with history, HistoryDone, dropped events, rescans, root changes and ID wraps told as named Lost subtrees - and how it compares with watchman's FSEvents watcher, which never resumes across a restart.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/linux.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal/linux.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 restore on Linux: the statx sweep of tracked paths on a per-core pool beside blaze-core's ring, its speed of light, and the journal effect on fanotify or inotify.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/journal.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-journal - a warm restart takes what changed from the OS's journal (FSEvents from a saved event ID, NTFS's USN from a saved USN, Linux's statx sweep of the saved stamp column) and reads and hashes only files whose stamp moved; lost journals are named and rescan only their subtree. The VFS side (blaze-vfs's watcher and disk column), its speed of light, how it compares with git, watchman, Everything and Bazel, and which test proves what.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/image.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/image.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2's daemon state is one mapped image (crates/blaze-image) opened by one BLAKE3 of its spine, every 64 KiB group checked by a hardware CRC32C on first touch and named when corrupt, with symbols and interned values as mapped tables whose u32 IDs survive restarts and a GC that never renumbers a live one.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast — where the front end's time goes, area by area (name resolution, expansion, trait goals, method probing, inference, bodies, const eval, MIR building, borrowck): the work's lower bound, what v2's code does as of 2026-10-29, the faster design with its prior art, and which child builds it.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-trait.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-trait.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-trait — trait goals answered before canonicalization (a per-revision global-goal table keyed by packed IDs), a shape table for Copy, Clone and auto traits over a per-ADT verdict, and the persistent goal cache by content; the bound, today's cost, the design, and why each keeps rustc's answers.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-trait-store.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-trait-store.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-trait-store — the persistent trait-goal cache by content (compile-time.md change 17): a global goal's answer kept in the store under its stable form, with the facts its evaluation read, reused while every fact hashes the same and the solver matches; the bound, the design, what no read can express yet, and the requests.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-mir.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-mir.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-mir — MIR building's cost per HIR node against its bound, counted from hir-ty-mir's lower.rs and lower/; the quadratic unwind and scope-exit paths replaced by rustc's cached unwind block per scope (lower/unwind.rs), the match tree's quadratic candidate handling, and the differential and allocation tests that prove the MIR is the same.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-method.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-method.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-method's notes for method resolution (fast.md section 3): traits in scope as interned IDs and per-name buckets, a lock-free pick cache shared by a crate's bodies in a revision through capture_reads/replay_reads, a cache of autoderef steps by canonical receiver, the bound with its arithmetic, and every rustc rule the probe keeps.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-infer.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-infer.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-infer — inference within a body (fast.md section 4). Coercion by head dispatch (one snapshot or none where rustc's order can't fall back, the unsizing attempt skipped where no candidate exists or the same attempt already failed) and watch lists for stalled obligations (a round visits only obligations whose variables were written), each proved equal to rustc's order case by case, with the differential test, the cases and the allocation budgets that check it.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-const.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-const.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-const — constants of the closed shape (integer, bool and char literals, paths to other constants, checked arithmetic, integer casts, size_of/align_of, array lengths) evaluated over HIR with the MIR evaluator's exact bytes and errors; every other constant by MIR evaluation; dependencies' constants served by content from the global cache.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-const-deps.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-const-deps.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-const-deps — a dependency's `const` item with no generic arguments, once evaluated, is kept in the store (and so the global cache) under its crate's check-result key, its stable item key and the encoding's version, as its bytes and a type with no salsa id; `const_eval_query` asks for it before reading the body, and a miss records the value for the driver to write after the build.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-borrowck.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-borrowck.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-borrowck — borrow checking's dataflow redone to its bound: rows chosen by size (dense up to 16 words, line-slotted above), sparse gen/kill, difference propagation in the fixpoint, one decoding pass into fact columns with a place-type column, cache before folding, every per-body buffer in the body's frame; NLL over the columns kept against a Datalog join.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-bodies — which bodies are checked, where and when (fast.md section 5): every crate-wide read a body makes, audited from the code and narrowed so an edit re-infers only the bodies it can change; bodies as plane tasks, reached ones first; a dependency's check outcome computed once for everyone.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies-tasks.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies-tasks.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-bodies-tasks — a check as one plane task per body and one per file module for its items, slots read in def-map order so the output is the same whatever ran first; a build tells the check the bodies its codegen reaches as the walk finds them, and those are checked first, while the unit's outcome still waits for every body.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies-cache.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies-cache.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-bodies-cache — a dependency's check computed once for everyone: its crate-level outcome (diagnostics as the build shows them, failed or not) and, per body, the inference result and borrowck verdict codegen reads, in stable form, filed beside frontend-deps' image under the image's key and what else the check reads.
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies-cache-bodies.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/fast-bodies-cache-bodies.md) (2026-10-29): frontend-fast-bodies-cache-bodies — per body of a dependency crate, its InferenceRecord with every id relocated through a table and its borrowck verdict, in one blaze_format part beside frontend-deps' image, read back in another process (crates/hir-ty/src/check_cache.rs).
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/deps.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/deps.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 reads dependency crates from images of their def map, lang items and signatures keyed by every input, parses only the bodies codegen or const eval asks for, and reparses and re-lowers only the items an edit touches (frontend.md items 5 and 14).
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/db.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/db.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2's front end has one concrete database, base_db::Db, passed as &Db to every query (rustc's TyCtxt design on salsa), so a query call is static and a memo hit is a chain of loads with no call through a vtable or function pointer (frontend.md item 15).
- [v2/plan/lanes/frontend/activate.md](v2/plan/lanes/frontend/activate.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2's daemon is socket-activated by launchd and systemd from one typed unit description, takes the socket it is passed or stops naming why, and proof's budgets time restart to first answer after a clean stop and after kill -9 on blaze itself.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-unsafe-front-intern.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-unsafe-front-intern.md) (2026-10-29): intern, span, tt, mbe, syntax-bridge and const-ast under unsafe.md: intern's unsafe gathered into two modules with safe APIs under a deny root, span's hygiene made safe, what each remaining unsafe buys, the untrusted-bytes checks of a restored table, the reference and model tests, and the fuzz target filed for the table section.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-syntax.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-syntax.md) (2026-10-29): speed-syntax: the lexer, parser and reparse of crates/parser and crates/syntax against simdjson, Zig, tree-sitter and rowan; what changed and what is left.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span.md) (2026-10-29): speed pass on the format lane's span, token tree, macro and interner crates; benchmarks named, before and after.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span-tt.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span-tt.md) (2026-10-29): speed-span-tt — tt's storage as flat columns (8-byte nodes, CSR subtrees, packed spans in a side column, canonical so equality is a memcmp) and syntax-bridge as one preallocated pass with no String per token; benchmarks, before, changes, after.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span-mbe.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span-mbe.md) (2026-10-29): speed-span-mbe — the macro_rules matcher, fragment parsing and transcriber in crates/mbe brought to the v2 speed bar against rustc's macro_parser; benchmark, before, changes, after.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span-ast.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-span-ast.md) (2026-10-29): speed-span-ast — span's ast id maps, real and expansion span maps, and const-ast brought to the v2 speed bar; benchmarks, before, changes, after.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-of-light.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-of-light.md) (2026-10-29): lane format's speed of light: the bound each component's work and the hardware set, the arithmetic, and how the design reaches 90% of it.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-ids-format.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-ids-format.md) (2026-10-29): speed pass on blaze-ids and blaze-format (content IDs, interner, zero-copy records, column tiers); the techniques each matches, and where it falls short of the best and why.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir.md) (2026-10-29): speed-hir's index for lane format: hir-def's expression store and item tree as columns, measured against Zig's ZIR/AIR, Carbon's SemIR and rustc's arena HIR; headline before/after per part, speed-of-light verdicts and what is left.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-store.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-store.md) (2026-10-29): The HIR expression store as columns (exprs, pats, type refs, source maps), lowering that allocates per body, and how it compares with Zig's ZIR/AIR, Carbon's SemIR and rustc's arena HIR.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-store-readers.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-store-readers.md) (2026-10-29): speed pass of the expression store's readers in hir-def (expr scopes as columns, a body's anchor maps shared by its anchor, the invalidation tests).
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-store-lower.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-store-lower.md) (2026-10-29): speed-hir-store-lower — body and signature lowering (`ExprCollector`) moved onto the pass-2 HIR store: child lists on the builder's list stacks, forward source maps pushed, owned paths moved into side tables; ids and order unchanged.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-items.md](v2/plan/lanes/format/speed-hir-items.md) (2026-10-29): The item tree as columns (9 bytes an item plus a payload record of 1 to 16), lowering that allocates per file from a reused per-worker builder, and how it compares with Zig's ZIR declarations, Carbon's SemIR name scopes and rustc's arena HIR.
- [v2/plan/lanes/format.md](v2/plan/lanes/format.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: data formats: IDs, zero-copy records, flat syntax, side tables.

- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/stencil-patch.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/stencil-patch.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 lane fastcompile, child fastcompile-stencil-patch of stencil.md: the patcher in crates/blaze-stencil (patch.rs, patch/, buf.rs, code.rs, enc.rs), its passes (scan, select, slots, frame, edges, size, emit, finish) and the columns each writes, the slot area's layout with the glue's scratch and the relay slots, how edges, fusions, accumulators, traps and constants are written, what is an error, the tests against a mock library and glue, and where it is faster or slower than Xu and Kjolstad's copy-and-patch, CPython's JIT, TPDE and Cranelift's fastalloc.
- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/stencil-gen.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/stencil-gen.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 lane fastcompile, child fastcompile-stencil-gen of stencil.md: the generator in crates/blaze-stencil/gen (run by build.rs) that has LLVM make every stencil at blaze's build time, how each hole is made in the IR per instruction set, the checks that refuse a stencil, the probe of the pinned registers, the library's reader and PTHash index, and how it compares with CPython's JIT and Xu and Kjolstad's generator.
- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/speed-of-light.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/speed-of-light.md) (2026-10-29): lane fastcompile's speed of light: the bound each component's work and the hardware set, the arithmetic, and how far the design is from it. An index to every component's bound, then the stencil patcher's cost per IR instruction and the library reader's.
- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/share.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/share.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 fastcompile idea 2, shared code across generic instances (crates/hir-ty-share): the share key, a salsa query over the generic and monomorphized MIR that is equal for two instances exactly when their code is; what it reads, why it is sound, the state of the art (mergefunc, COMDAT folding, ICF, Swift, .NET, Go, polymorphization) and why deciding before codegen beats folding after.
- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/select.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/select.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 lane fastcompile, idea 3 (exact test selection): what exists in blaze-usercode, what is missing (executed versus reached, keys that miss which function a call binds to, the cached mark), crates/blaze-testsel's executed record, function table and selection over identity and bound code, the hooks requested from usercode, lazy, codegen, items, ci and cargo, the exactness argument and tests, and the state of the art it beats.
- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/sched.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/sched.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 lane fastcompile, ideas 11 and 12 (scheduling from history; blaze built with PGO and BOLT): crates/blaze-history, its fixed-size per-key records in a seqlock table that readers never lock, persisted in the daemon image; the `Predict` hook the plane asks; tools/pgo, which trains, builds, BOLTs, gates and publishes blaze through blaze; and the state of the art each matches or beats.

- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/macros.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/macros.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 fastcompile change 20 (crates/blaze-macro-eval): proc macros run as their own code with the real `proc_macro` client on the MIR evaluator, in process, answered by blaze's server, every access checked; the expanders behind `load`, the key that misses no input, state across calls, the learned session verdict, isolation, the state of the art, and the speed of light of a hit and a run.
- [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/macros-tier.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/macros-tier.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 lane fastcompile, change 20's second tier (crates/blaze-macro-eval/src/tier.rs and src/tier/): a proc-macro crate compiled by copy-and-patch from hir-ty-codegen's Cranelift IR and run in blaze's process, isolated as a wasm engine isolates a module. - [v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/hashcons.md](v2/plan/lanes/fastcompile/hashcons.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 lane fastcompile, idea 5 (hash-consing of query values): crates/blaze-hashcons, its sharded append-only interner with lock-free reads, fingerprints computed once at intern, persistence by content, the hooks in blaze-query and salsa, and the state of the art it matches or beats.

- [v2/plan/design/restore.md](v2/plan/design/restore.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the daemon restores from disk instantly: a mapped image with no deserializing, IDs stable across restarts, changed files known from the OS's journal, and work paged in on demand.
- [v2/plan/design/prior-art.md](v2/plan/design/prior-art.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 borrows from Flecs, ECS and game engines: shapes, sparse overrides, relationship pairs, table change counters, archetype batching, fiber jobs, frame graphs, command buffers, LOD-style tiers, streaming, Live++-style hot reload, Tracy-style markers.
- [v2/plan/design/model.md](v2/plan/design/model.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the machine model: one warm VM, branches as views.
- [v2/plan/design/memory.md](v2/plan/design/memory.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 manages memory like a game engine: allocators by lifetime (frame, request, view, image), virtual-memory-reserved arenas with stable addresses, pools, generational handles, per-subsystem budgets, and zero general-purpose allocations in the warm loop.
- [v2/plan/design/hardware.md](v2/plan/design/hardware.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: hardware acceleration, and why no GPU.
- [v2/plan/design/frontend.md](v2/plan/design/frontend.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: what rust-analyzer's front end got wrong for a compiler, and what v2 does instead: incremental name resolution, indexed impls, one token format, signature-only dependencies, mapped files, no IDE-only work.
- [v2/plan/design/data.md](v2/plan/design/data.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: data-oriented layout and compression in every stage.
- [v2/plan/design/concurrency.md](v2/plan/design/concurrency.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: how threads share data: reads never lock or write shared memory, values are immutable once published, task boundaries reclaim memory, no build lock.
- [v2/plan/design/compile-time.md](v2/plan/design/compile-time.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the bigger changes for the fastest compile times: reachability-only codegen, a persistent trait cache, the nightly's own solver, proc macros on our own compiler, tiered compilation and idle cores always working, lazy per-function compilation, copy-and-patch codegen, no link and no rewrite for dev runs, one global cache, semantic edits and declared intent, shared generic code, exact test selection, hash-consing, premapped dependencies, scheduling from history, PGO and BOLT.
- [v2/plan.md](v2/plan.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2: the plan, as an index. Start here; each line links to the detail.
- [v2-vfs.md](v2-vfs.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 vfs lane's design: the Merkle tree, heads and views, rebase, the journal with group commit, recovery and compaction, and the disk watcher as one input of transactions.
- [v2-store.md](v2-store.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2's store as written by the store lane: the files of a store directory, how a group commit survives a crash, hot and cold values, chunks, placing, verification, layers, and the remote tier.
- [v2-codegen.md](v2-codegen.md) (2026-10-29): blaze v2 codegen lane's design: per-function units, instance keys, templates (the back-end memo up to callee renaming), code dedupe, folding by constants, settings and tiering, release summaries and imports.
- [unit-keys.md](unit-keys.md) (2026-10-29): The store is never wholly cold: each record keyed by what its value depends on, so a new pin or a sandbox change reuses what it did not change.
- [memory-budget.md](memory-budget.md) (2026-10-29): Memory as a scheduled budget: blaze reads the machine's real limit, admits work by its measured peak, sheds caches under pressure and stops with an error naming what cannot fit, never swapping a machine to death.
- [linker.md](linker.md) (2026-10-28): blaze's own linker: one patch engine with a lasting layout, writing to a running process or an executable, replacing cc, lld, ld64 and link.exe.
- [future/const-macros.md](future/const-macros.md) (2026-10-28): Const macros: proc macros written inline as const fn, run by the const evaluator. Stage 0 is experimental.
- [driver.md](driver.md) (2026-10-28): The build driver as a graph that does no IO: what is wrong with the serial driver and what replaces it.
- [remote-cache.md](remote-cache.md) (2026-10-27): One shared remote cache for CI and everyone: the gateway, the CAS API, and the slices built and to come.
- [closure.md](closure.md) (2026-10-27): The closure build scripts run with: what is fetched and laid out (built), and the mount namespace (not yet).
- [self-contained.md](self-contained.md) (2026-10-25): blaze self-contained: one curl install that builds any Cargo project with no rustup, toolchain or cargo.
- [roadmap.md](roadmap.md) (2026-10-24): blaze-next, the floor of an edit for agents: content-addressed VFS, VM forks, sans-IO core, the agent API.
- [ci-runner.md](ci-runner.md) (2026-10-24): A CI runner on ix VMs: a warm blaze VM per repository and a fork per branch. Design, nothing built.

## Records

Research, reports and measurements, true on their date and not brought up to date. Newest first.

- [v2/plan/lanes/concurrency/shared-structures.md](v2/plan/lanes/concurrency/shared-structures.md) (2026-11-01): Step 2 of the locks brief (2026-11-01) - each shared map, locked collector and locked queue either moved to papaya (blaze_hash::SharedMap), crossbeam's SegQueue/ArrayQueue or par's ordered results, or kept as a lock, with the reason.
- [v2/plan/lanes/concurrency/flights.md](v2/plan/lanes/concurrency/flights.md) (2026-11-01): Flights under contention (crates/blaze-graph/benches/flights.rs, 2026-11-01, busy Mac). parking_lot's sharded map is 1.5x std's uncontended and 3-5x on one lock; the current lock-free table matches parking_lot on one thread and is 3x it at 18 threads; the first open-addressed table was flat at 13 Mops/s (shared counter, rebuilds).
